# Skeleton

<!-- Generated by `pnpm readme:build`. Edit only inside the hand-written block. -->

media and display · tier 1 · beta · renders on the server and ships no client JavaScript.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

As the placeholder that holds a page's shape while its content loads, most often as a
`<Suspense>` fallback. Pick the shape of what is coming - lines of text, an avatar circle, a
control-height rectangle or a card - and give it the real dimensions through `className`,
because a placeholder that reserves the wrong size is a layout shift when the content lands.

```tsx
<Suspense fallback={<Skeleton rows={5} />}>
  <InvoiceNotes />
</Suspense>

<div className="flex items-center gap-4">
  <Skeleton variant="circle" className="size-12" />
  <Skeleton rows={2} className="w-48 text-lg" />
</div>
```

The text shape is exactly as tall as the lines it replaces at any type step: each row is the
font size high and its margins make up the line height, so set the type step on it as you
would on the text. `rows` is clamped between 1 and 50. Every shape is hidden from assistive
technology, so mark the loading region itself, for example with `aria-busy`.

<!-- /hand-written -->

## Import

```tsx
import { Skeleton } from 'topclassui/skeleton'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rows` | no | `integer`, min 1, max 50 | `3` | How many lines the text shape holds, clamped to the bounds; the other shapes ignore it. |
| `variant` | no | `text` \| `circle` \| `rect` \| `card` | `"text"` | The shape it holds the place of: lines of text, a circle, a rectangle or a card. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
